title: Sandy Dennis is absolutely breathtaking. How come she isn't more known? Her performance in "That Cold Day in the Park" is obsession at its most subtle.

commenti.body:
Haven't seen A Cold Day in the Park but yea, absolutely agree. Jimmy Dean and Virginia Woolf alone. One of the best actors I've ever seen. Fun in The Out-of-Towners too. Didn't love The Fox but she's at least good in it.

Almost like John Cazale. Both died tragically young but everything they did was masterful.

I absolutely love “That Cold Day in the Park.” Really under-appreciated piece of work. Really wish she’d been given more leading roles — her body of work is frustratingly small for how talented she was.

She's terrific. As much I'm impressed with her work in *That Cold Day in the Park*, *Who's Afraid of Virginia Wolf?* and *Up the Down Staircase*, her scene under the bridge in *The Out-of-Towners* is the single funniest scene I have ever seen in my life. Chef's kiss.

What about her one scene in Another Woman as Gena Rowlands' put-upon friend? So good. As brilliant as Gena Rowlands was in that movie, Sandy Dennis has the best scene in the movie. Going from fake surprise and joy to subtle resentment until she goes off. Her monologue being a confession of anger, jealousy, suspicion and even doubt.

I thought she adopted some strange affectations later in her career. She wasn’t everyone’s cup of tea. 

This from her NYT obituary: 

The New Yorker film critic Pauline Kael once complained that Ms. Dennis “has made an acting style of postnasal drip,” an assessment Ms. Dennis herself said was correct and worked to change.
I never noticed all that much but if people were annoyed by that, imagine with Meryl Streep and her out of breath mannerisms. Or Bette Davis sounding like she was dubbing a Russian movie.

I think she came around when there were a lot of great actresses that were probably more talented and versatile than she was. I thought she still was very good, though. She’s what people incorrectly think Kristen Stewart is.
